manifest.hypothesis: A clear, short cue after a missed pair will help local players recognize which seat acts next without obscuring the board or changing match rules.
kill_criteria: Blind playtest participants still cannot identify the next player after a miss or misread a match as a handoff.
The cue obscures playable tiles or controls, creates problematic motion, or cannot be understood with assistive technology.
The change delays or duplicates legal actions, changes scoring/turn order, or breaks bot play, pause, restart, or save restore.
The implementation requires edits outside games/flip-match/** or degrades the game's core responsiveness.
success_criteria: After a miss settles, the interface explicitly names the previous and next seats, with the next seat also identifiable by color-independent text, before the next action; players in a blind playtest can identify who acts next.
After a successful match, the same player continues and no handoff cue appears.
Pause, dialogs, restart, and save restore do not show a stale cue or allow a prior game's cue to affect the new game.
The cue is readable on desktop, phone, and iPad portrait and landscape views and does not prevent legal tile actions or bot turns.
manifest.title: Flip & Match turn handoff cue
